My land is about 5 mu. I have been farming this same ground for over twenty years, first with my mother-in-law watching, then on my own. My husband helps when he is back from the city, but mostly it is me. I do not read much, so I go by what I see, what my neighbors do, and what the seed shop man tells me every spring.

In Quzhou, everybody plants wheat in autumn and maize after the wheat comes off. That is what my family always did. The soil knows this rhythm and so do I. I am not going to change it. The wheat feeds us through the year — we sell most of it to the grain station — and the maize either gets sold or fed to the chickens if the price is bad.

For wheat I will use the improved variety the co-op recommended last year. My neighbor got good yields with it. For maize I always buy hybrid seed from the county seed shop — the hybrid is stronger and fills out better, everyone switched years ago.

I water the wheat four times: before winter comes in, again at the cold break, at jointing, and at heading. If I miss the heading water the ears go thin and I lose money. For maize I only water twice — once at tasseling if it looks dry and once when the kernels are filling.

Fertilizer: I apply what my husband's uncle told me is the right amount. Maybe a little more on the wheat because the field in the west corner always looks pale in spring. I buy compound fertilizer plus urea at the supply shop and follow what they write on the bag, more or less.

I spray the wheat twice — once for weeds early on and once for aphids before heading. Maize gets two sprays too, for the corn borer and a herbicide after emergence.

I do rotary tillage before wheat planting. For maize I just seed directly into the stubble right after I harvest the wheat — no time to plough and the ground is still soft.
